skill://dispatch and skill://dispatch-first: any ask or comment the implementer writes on INFRA-250 goes through them, and a finding outside the issue is an ask rather than a new issue.

skill://legion-worker/references/pr-body.md: the tester drives the changed surface in its own pod turn and reads CI for gofmt, the contracts check and the unit lanes rather than rerunning them; its E2E (tester) line and proof array come from here.

findings.finding: F1 - acceptance 1 ('no test skipped for want of a container runtime') covers more than NATS: internal/dispatch/files (SeaweedFS), three docker pause sites, internal/dispatch/pmdoc (repository-root bun install) and every Postgres-gated skip also fail or skip in a pod.
findings.answer: Measured the whole suite in the pod (plan section 1.1): 56 ok, 22 FAIL, classified by cause. Put the four classes to the architect with a recommendation; it approved and rewrote the spec to version 6, whose acceptance 1 now claims only the packages failing for want of a NATS server and requires the residue to be named in the pull request body. Plan section 6 A1 states the exact command, the pass condition and the residue; the three docker pause sites are inside this issue and become Server.Freeze (plan sections 4.1, 4.2, T4).

findings.finding: F2 - acceptance 2 ('no change in what it covers') cannot hold for the two-image matrix: testnats.Images runs tests against nats:2.10 and the hub's pinned 2.15.1 digest, and one compiled-in server is one version.
findings.answer: Plan section 4.3 keeps StartImageConfig and the matrix container-backed in files tagged //go:build natslive, which the pod run never compiles and the envoy-infra-go job already passes. The three matrix tests in internal/testnats/nats_test.go move to a tagged file, and the envoy-go job gains one step (go test -tags natslive ./internal/testnats/) so they keep running. The plan-reviewer confirmed envoy-infra-go compiles the tagged file through infra/core/nats_auth_live_test.go:104 and infra/seed/seed_live_test.go:39.

findings.finding: F3 - the in-process switch needs seams the spec does not name: pause, a monitoring port, the server log, SIGHUP reload, restart keeping the store, store directories and TestMain shutdown.
findings.answer: Each one is answered in plan section 4.2's table and was proved in the pod before the plan was written (section 1.2): random client and monitoring ports through Port/HTTPPort -1 with ClientURL and MonitorAddr, SetLoggerV2 for the -DV trace and the violation lines, ReloadOptions returning its own refusal reason, Shutdown plus a new server on the same StoreDir for the restart, and a relay that stops copying bytes in place of docker pause.

findings.finding: F4 - 'one entry point, no helper can bypass it' has three bypasses today (internal/bus/name_test.go, cmd/natstail/main_test.go, internal/store/interest_markers_test.go call tcnats.Run themselves) plus three docker pause sites, and no machine check.
findings.answer: All six move onto the rig in T4. Plan section 4.1 adds the guard test the analyst proposed: it walks go list -deps of the module and fails when a package outside internal/testnats imports testcontainers' modules/nats, or when a test file names exec.Command("docker" or NewDockerClientWithOpts. cmd/dispatch/settings_test.go:46-141 is the in-repository precedent cited.

findings.finding: F5 - acceptance 4 deletes files that are not on main: local.go and ENVOY_TEST_NATS_BIN arrive with pull request sjawhar/legion#2167 (INFRA-141), still open.
findings.answer: Confirmed on the base commit. The architect instructed planning against a tree where #2167 has merged and keeping none of them. Plan section 4.5 says so, T1 rebases onto the current main, and A4's check passes either way with the pull-request body saying which case held.

findings.finding: F6 - five CI steps sed the Image/HubImage constants out of the source, and envoy-e2e-local seds the docker run line out of e2e-local.sh and exits 1 when it finds none.
findings.answer: Plan section 4.3 keeps Image, HubImage and Images as untagged single-line constants so the five pre-pull steps are untouched. Plan section 4.4 and T5 delete the envoy-e2e-local 'Pull the NATS image the script starts' step and that job's E2E_NATS_CONTAINER, because the docker run line it reads is gone.

findings.finding: F7 - acceptance 3 has unmet prerequisites beyond docker: openssl may be absent from the worker image, and the script's bun stages need a repository-root install; e2e-local.test.sh asserts the docker call log.
findings.answer: Measured: /usr/bin/openssl, bun, curl, go and jq are all present in this pod. Plan section 4.4 records that, has A3 quote command -v for all five, makes bun install an explicit step of the A3 proof, and lists e2e-local.test.sh and scripts/README.md among T5's files.

findings.finding: F8 - 'the testcontainers dependency leaves the Go suite' is false: internal/testpg, internal/tests3 and internal/smoke keep it.
findings.answer: Recorded as the plan's one departure from the spec (plan section 2, and specDepartures below). Only modules/nats becomes reachable from tagged files alone; testcontainers-go stays a direct requirement of packages/envoy/go.mod.

findings.finding: F9 - the new dependency lands in three modules and two workspace sums, not one.
findings.answer: T1 names every file: packages/envoy/go.mod, packages/envoy/go.sum, packages/envoy/infra/go.sum, packages/daemon/go.sum and go.work.sum, and ends with the daemon's build and vet green. The risk list records that packages/daemon compiles the dependency through testnatsimages.

findings.finding: F10 - acceptance 5 has no artefact a test-only dependency can change: no committed Go notices file, and every go-third-party-notices.sh call names production packages.
findings.answer: Put to the architect, which approved and rewrote the criterion: the command still exits 0 and its output is byte-identical to main's. A5 runs it on both refs for ./cmd/listener and for the two envoy-infra commands and diffs them.

findings.finding: F11 - 'the whole packages/envoy Go test suite' is four different runs; each criterion needs a reading.
findings.answer: A1 names the exact pod command and the separate ./internal/integration run; A2 names the eight CI jobs that must be green by run id; A3 names envoy-e2e-local as the script's CI coverage.

findings.finding: F12 - wall clock and the 10-minute per-package default are unaddressed for a 2-CPU pod, and the in-process server moves the server's CPU and memory into the test binary.
findings.answer: The baseline run of section 1.1 completed in this pod with no package hitting the default deadline (slowest: cmd/agent-secrets 449s, internal/dispatch/pmdoc 339s), so A1 keeps the same command and deadline for comparability. The risk list has T2 report the shared server's start cost and peak RSS for internal/bus and cmd/listener, and tune firstAccounts only if the measurement says to.

findings.finding: F13 - three spec claims do not trace (the tree state, the fifteen-test count and its sources, the touched-package list), the Kubernetes RBAC sentence is unverified, and the already-documented pinned-binary route (INFRA-113, INFRA-117) is not weighed against the library.
findings.answer: Plan section 1.4 weighs the binary route against the library and says why the library wins here (go run fetches at run time, which acceptance 1 forbids; a hand-supplied binary is what acceptance 4 deletes), citing both solution pages. Plan sections 4.5 and 2 correct the tree state and the dependency claim. The touched-package list is replaced by T4's call-site inventory, which includes cmd/listener/restart_test.go, internal/dispatch/startup, internal/kvwatch and the whole packages/envoy/infra module. The RBAC sentence is the spec's and not relied on by any plan step.

specDepartures.spec: 'What would close it' says that once the in-process server lands, 'the testcontainers dependency leaves the Go suite'.
specDepartures.plan: Only github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go/modules/nats becomes reachable from build-tagged files alone. github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-go stays a direct requirement of packages/envoy/go.mod, and the plan does not try to remove it.
specDepartures.evidence: internal/testpg/testpg.go:10-11 (pgvector, used by infra/core/dispatch_permissions_live_test.go), internal/tests3/seaweedfs.go:17-18 (SeaweedFS, used by internal/dispatch/files/s3_server_test.go) and internal/smoke/listener_test.go:24-27 (the listener image beside NATS on a Docker network) all import it, and none of the three is in this issue's scope: the architect ruled the S3 test out, and smoke is its own CI job.
